newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: OAU supports Ethiopian-backed Somali peace pact.
newsitem.headline: OAU supports Ethiopian-backed Somali peace pact.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) said on Thursday it supported a declaration by 26 Somali factions to work for peace and had earmarked $430,000 for its implementation.
Following the submission by an Ethiopian representative of a project proposal, the OAU expressed strong support for the peace process which began with eight weeks of talks in Sodere, Ethiopia.
"It has also decided to earmark the sum of $430,000 from the OAU Peace Fund to assist in the implementation of the provisions of the Somalia reconciliation project," the OAU statement added.
Twenty-six Somali faction leaders agreed in Sodere in early January to set up a National Salvation Council to establish a provisional government for Somalia.
But powerful Somali faction leader Hussein Aideed, who says he is Somalia's president, refused to attend the talks and denounced the agreement as Ethiopian meddling in Somali affairs.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991. Warlords then turned their guns on each other, fuelling a famine that killed 300,000 people.
